title: Bees: open-source AI agents that run on your own computer
excerpt: Run agentic teams from your own computer while your agents, files, browser sessions, cookies, and passwords stay local.
content_html:
Run agentic teams from your own computer.

Your agents, files, browser sessions and passwords stay on your machine. Use a local model, or the Claude Code and Codex subscriptions you already pay for. Bees adds no fee per token or per run.

Free and open source for macOS, Windows and Linux.

Local agents. Shared processes. Human control.

  • Free, open-source desktopMIT or Apache 2.0. Add cloud coordination when your team needs it.
  • Local-first executionFiles, logins, indexes and run folders stay on your machines.
  • No Bees AI feesUse local models, subscriptions you already have, or your own API keys.
  • Private or sharedStay on one computer, or work across teammates and devices.
  • Work that survivesStages, retries and recovery, so a long job picks up where it stopped.
  • You stay in chargeAgents ask questions and wait for approval before risky actions.
  • Clear routingEach run follows a visible graph built from what actually happened.
  • Agents that improveScheduled agents learn only from the feedback you give them.
  • Company BrainLocal search over the company files you already keep.
  • The right model per roleGive each agent the model and tools that fit its job.

One request, start to finish.

  1. Describe the work

    Tell Ask Bees what you need in plain English, like reviewing vendor contracts every Monday.

  2. Bees plans the team

    It proposes the agents, stages, tools and schedule. Nothing runs until you apply it.

  3. Agents work on your computer

    They read files, use the browser and write results in their own run folder on your machine.

  4. A reviewer checks it

    A separate agent reviews the work before it moves on, and sends it back if it falls short.

  5. You make the final call

    Bees stops and asks before anything leaves, like sending an email or publishing a post.

Three things to try first.

Summarize Hacker News in a minute

Ask Bees to browse Hacker News and get back today's stories grouped into news, Show HN and Ask HN.

Hand a task to a teammate's laptop

Start a task on your computer and let it finish on a teammate's. The files stay on the machine that did the work. Only the progress syncs.

Draft email replies on a schedule

A scheduled process reads new Gmail messages and drafts replies. You read them and decide what gets sent.

Bees Cloud never receives or stores your files.

Bees keeps the work separate from the coordination. Regular organizations sync only what keeps people and agents in step. Your documents stay in storage you control.

Stays on your computer

  • Document files and their contents
  • Model keys and passwords
  • Agent runs, inside their own folder
  • Real file paths on your disk

Can sync, in Regular organizations

  • Teams and who belongs to them
  • Process runs and their stages
  • Who has claimed which work
  • File names and relative paths, never contents

Want no third party at all? Pick a local model and local tools, and Bees runs fully offline. Otherwise, selected content goes from your machine straight to the AI providers you set up, not through Bees Cloud. See what leaves your computer for each setup.

Start alone. Bring your team later.

Regular organization

Free to start

Sign in, create teams and invite people. Progress syncs while files and runs stay on each person's computer.

  • Shared agents and process templates
  • Shared runs, assignments and claims
  • Work across several machines
  • Invite teammates any time
Create a Regular organization

Private organization

Free local edition

For work that must stay on one computer. No Bees account or cloud connection needed.

  • Unlimited teams, agents and processes
  • Works offline and air-gapped
  • Local or cloud models
  • Cannot add team members later
Create a Private organization

Privacy you can check, not just read about.

The Bees desktop app is open source under MIT or Apache 2.0. Read how it handles your files, change it to fit, and run it where you want.
